sources.shortCitation: BN, Odeon O. 236842 — “Ninon, ach uśmiechnij się!” / “Signorina, signorina” (Kiepura)
sources.fullCitation: “Ninon, ach uśmiechnij się! : z f-mu «Zdobyć cię muszę». Signorina, signorina : z f-mu «Zdobyć cię muszę» / B. Kaper, W. Jurmann ; M. Halicz.” Jan Kiepura, vocal, with the Odeon symphony orchestra. Warsaw: Polskie Zakłady Fonograficzne “Odeon”, [post 1930]. One 78 rpm disc, 25 cm, publisher's number O. 236842. Biblioteka Narodowa, Magazyn Zbiorów Dźwiękowych i Audiowizualnych, shelfmark Fon.II.11.690; MMS ID 991034500969705066, OCLC 899876292. Language given as Polish, genre as film music. Marcella Halicz is credited “Sł.”, that is for the words. Accessed 2 August 2026.
sources.title: Ninon, ach uśmiechnij się! / Signorina, signorina — Odeon O. 236842
sources.creator: Jan Kiepura, vocal; Odeon orchestra

sources.shortCitation: Odeon O-11811, “Mein Gorilla hat 'ne Villa im Zoo” (recorded Berlin, 13 February 1933)
sources.fullCitation: Hans Albers with the Odeon-Künstler-Orchester under Otto Dobrindt. “Mein Gorilla hat 'ne Villa im Zoo.” Paso doble. Odeon O-11811, matrix Be 10227-2, 1933. Digital transfer on YouTube; session data consulted in the Odeon label list at musiktiteldb.de. Accessed 15 August 2026.
sources.title: Mein Gorilla hat 'ne Villa im Zoo — Odeon O-11811
sources.creator: Hans Albers, with the Odeon-Künstler-Orchester under Otto Dobrindt
sources.researchNote: The uploader's description supplies the matrix number; the label is not shown. The recording date, take, studio and April 1933 release follow the Odeon label list at musiktiteldb.de. The companion side, matrix Be 10226, survives in a filmed-label transfer and is documented as part of the same session.

sources.shortCitation: Odeon O-11811 a, “Immer wenn ich glücklich bin” (recorded Berlin, 13 February 1933)
sources.fullCitation: Hans Albers with the Odeon-Künstler-Orchester under Otto Dobrindt. “Immer wenn ich glücklich bin.” Foxtrot from the Boston sound film Heut’ kommt’s drauf an; label credits music to Walter Jurmann and B. Kaper and words to Fritz Rotter. Odeon O-11811 a, matrix Be 10226, 78 rpm, 1933. Filmed-label transfer published on YouTube by Schellackplatte on 21 May 2008. Accessed 15 August 2026.
sources.title: Immer wenn ich glücklich bin — Odeon O-11811 a
sources.creator: Hans Albers; Odeon-Künstler-Orchester, Otto Dobrindt, conductor
sources.researchNote: The recording date of 13 February 1933, Berlin studio 2, and the April 1933 release follow the Odeon label list at musiktiteldb.de. The filmed copy carries a C. A. Klemm dealer sticker and a notice prohibiting radio transmission without permission.

sources.fullCitation: Hans Albers with the Odeon-Künstler-Orchester conducted by O. Dobrindt. “Ich bin der Hans im Glück” / “In 24 Stunden.” Odeon O-11810, shellac, 10-inch, 78 rpm, Germany, 1933. Discogs release 28872088. Accessed 15 August 2026.
sources.title: Ich bin der Hans im Glück / In 24 Stunden — Odeon O-11 810
sources.creator: Hans Albers; Odeon-Künstler-Orchester, O. Dobrindt, conductor
sources.researchNote: Discogs identifies “In 24 Stunden” as matrix Be 10225-2 and the reverse as Be 10224. The recording date, take, Berlin studio and April 1933 release are independently supplied by the Odeon label list at musiktiteldb.de.

sources.shortCitation: Parlophone 80.235, “Was macht jede Nacht so ein kleines Baby in der Bar”
sources.fullCitation: Saxophon Orchester Dobbri, vocal by Max Mensing. “Was macht jede Nacht so ein kleines Baby in der Bar.” Slow fox; label credit “Fritz Rotter & Dr. B. Kaper”. Parlophone 80.235, matrix B 38451, n.d. Shellac disc, Radiomuseum Hardthausen / Schallarchiv; filmed-label transfer on YouTube. Accessed 20 August 2026.
sources.title: Was macht jede Nacht so ein kleines Baby in der Bar — Parlophone 80.235
sources.creator: Saxophon Orchester Dobbri, mit Gesang: Max Mensing
sources.date: n.d. [recorded in Berlin in 1930 according to the uploader]
sources.researchNote: The uploader dates the recording to Berlin in 1930 and describes the copy as a French Parlophone issue; neither statement is printed on the filmed label.

sources.fullCitation: “Otto Dobrindt.” Wikipedia (German). Records that he joined Carl Lindström AG in 1924 as a recording manager and became its chief recording manager, and that from 1925 he issued his own productions under pseudonyms including Saxophon-Orchester Dobbri, Odeon Tanz-Orchester, Wiener Bohème-Orchester, Dobbri, Robert Renard, Eddie Saxon, Frank Sandlers, Eric Harden and Götz Höhne; his orchestra accompanied Ufa stars on record, among them Hans Albers. Accessed 20 August 2026.
sources.title: Otto Dobrindt — Wikipedia (German)
sources.creator: Wikipedia contributors

sources.shortCitation: Odeon O-11439 a, “Ich weiß ein kleines Café”
sources.fullCitation: Austin Egen, accompanied by the Odeon-Tango-Orchester. “Ich weiß ein kleines Café.” Tango; label credits “Tango (Dr. B. Kaper und Austin Egen)” and “Text: Fritz Rotter”, with the note “Auch als Tanzplatte geeignet”. Odeon O-11439 a, matrix Be 9409, 78 R, B.I.E.M., with “Carl Lindström A.-G.” printed along the foot of the label, n.d. Label filmed in the YouTube upload by Ilja Livschakoff. Accessed 20 August 2026.
sources.title: Ich weiß ein kleines Café — Odeon O-11439 a
sources.creator: Austin Egen; Odeon-Tango-Orchester

sources.fullCitation: Jan Kiepura with the Odeon-Künstler-Orchester under Dr. Weissmann. “Ninon”, from the sound film Ein Lied für dich; music by Walter Jurmann and Dr. Bronislaw Kaper, words by Fritz Rotter and Ernst Marischka. Odeon red-label issue, 1933. YouTube transfer published by 78Upm. Accessed 20 August 2026.
sources.title: Ninon — Odeon, Jan Kiepura
sources.creator: Jan Kiepura; Odeon-Künstler-Orchester, Dr. Weissmann, conductor
sources.researchNote: The upload gives no catalogue number and does not show the disc label; the issue and credit details are therefore description-level evidence.

sources.fullCitation: König, Henry, comp. “Labelliste von „Odeon“ (1928–1933), Labelcode 00287: Odeon 78 rpm, Labelnummern von O-11000 bis O-11999.” musiktiteldb.de. 503 sides recorded, with matrix numbers, recording dates and studios, release months and parallel issues, compiled from the Discographie der deutschen Kleinkunst and related discographies; owner and manufacturer of the series given as Carl Lindström GmbH. Accessed 21 August 2026.
sources.title: Labelliste „Odeon“ (1928–1933), O-11000–O-11999
sources.creator: Henry König, compiler

sources.fullCitation: Tanz-Orchester Dajos Béla, vocal by Luigi Bernauer, credited on the label as Fred Lustig. “Signorina, ich liebe dich.” Tango; label credits Walter Jurmann, Bronislaw Kaper and Ernst Marischka. Odeon, n.d. Shellac disc, Radiomuseum Hardthausen / Schallarchiv; filmed-label transfer on YouTube. Accessed 21 August 2026.
sources.title: Signorina, ich liebe dich — Odeon
sources.creator: Tanz-Orchester Dajos Béla, Gesang: Luigi Bernauer, auf dem Etikett als Fred Lustig angegeben
sources.researchNote: The uploader associates the side with Hochzeitsreise zu dritt and dates the issue to 1932. The Odeon label list instead identifies the coupling as O-11768, matrix Be 10147, and places it in 1933. Because the filmed label carries no year, the date discrepancy remains unresolved.
